description:
observerEci computes the observer's Earth-centered position using a spherical-Earth model (radius = 6378.137 km, treating latitude as geocentric), producing wrong geocentric Cartesian coordinates for a WGS84 geodetic observer latitude. The downstream satellite look-angle pipeline (lookAngle → alt/az/range) then inherits this wrong observer position, producing systematically wrong alt/az values that diverge from true WGS84-based topocentric values.

Expected: observerEci should compute the observer's ECI position on the WGS84 ellipsoid surface (at sea level, h = 0 km): transform the WGS84 geodetic latitude/longitude to geocentric Cartesian coordinates via the standard ellipsoidal formulas using the WGS84 semi-major axis a = 6378.137 km and flattening f = 1/298.257223563.

Acceptance criteria:
- observerEci(jd, latRad, lonRad) computes the observer's geocentric ECI position using the WGS84 ellipsoid (a=6378.137 km, f=1/298.257223563) with the geodetic→geocentric Cartesian transform, not the spherical approximation a·cos(φ)·cos(λ), a·cos(φ)·sin(λ), a·sin(φ) [code-invariant: src/lib/satellite/look-angles.ts line 10: 'spherical Earth; ellipsoid/altitude refinement later' — the code names the simplification and marks it as pending. Line 26-30: the spherical-only implementation confirms this gap. The constant RE = 6378.137 km is the WGS84 semi-major axis a, used here as a spherical radius.]

Domain facts:
- WGS84: semi-major axis a = 6378.137 km (same as current RE), inverse flattening 1/f = 298.257223563, eccentricity² e² = 2f − f² ≈ 0.00669438
- Geodetic latitude φ → ellipsoid surface point (h=0): N(φ) = a / √(1 − e²·sin²(φ)); x = N(φ)·cos(φ)·cos(λ); y = N(φ)·cos(φ)·sin(λ); z = N(φ)·(1 − e²)·sin(φ)
- The current spherical model uses a spherical radius = a = 6378.137 km, which treats the input latRad as a geocentric latitude on a sphere — this is wrong for a WGS84 geodetic latitude input
- No concrete wrong alt/az values are known (reporter answered 'I don't know') — but the function's mathematical contract (compute observer position on Earth given a WGS84 geodetic lat/lon) is violated by the spherical approximation regardless of any specific consumer output
